models.title: Feedback Loops
models.description: Examine self-reinforcing (amplifying) and balancing (stabilizing) loops, and account for feedback delays that cause overshooting.

models.title: Theory of Constraints (Bottlenecks)
models.description: Any manageable system is limited in achieving more of its goals by a very small number of constraints. Optimizing non-bottlenecks is an illusion.

models.title: Tragedy of the Commons
models.description: Individuals with open access to a shared resource act independently according to their own self-interest, depleting or spoiling that resource.

models.title: Places to Intervene in a System
models.description: Meadows' 12-tier hierarchy of leverage points: parameters and buffers have low leverage; information flows, rules, goals, and paradigms have high leverage.

models.title: Second-Order Thinking
models.description: Thinking beyond immediate first-order payoffs to evaluate the downstream consequences, cascading ripples, and feedback reactions.

models.title: Inversion
models.description: Invert, always invert. Instead of asking how to succeed, identify and eliminate all paths that guarantee failure.

models.title: First Principles Reasoning
models.description: Boil things down to their most fundamental, irreducible truths and reason up from there, rather than reasoning by analogy.

models.title: Pre-Mortem Analysis
models.description: Assume the project has failed catastrophically 12 months in the future. Write the comprehensive post-mortem today to uncover hidden failure vectors.

models.title: Decision Reversibility (Two-Way Doors)
models.description: Distinguish between Type 1 (one-way doors, high consequence, irreversible) and Type 2 (two-way doors, low consequence, reversible) decisions.

models.title: Opportunity Cost
models.description: The true economic cost of choosing option X is the value of the best alternative foregone by not choosing it.

models.title: Chesterton's Fence
models.description: Do not remove a fence, rule, or constraint until you understand completely why it was put there in the first place.

models.title: Cynefin Framework
models.description: Classify problems into Clear (sense-categorize-respond), Complicated (sense-analyze-respond), Complex (probe-sense-respond), or Chaotic (act-sense-respond).

models.title: The Lindy Effect
models.description: For non-perishable entities (ideas, technologies, books), life expectancy is proportional to current age. Older surviving technologies outlast newer ones.

models.title: Via Negativa (Improvement by Subtraction)
models.description: Improvement is achieved by subtracting defects, removing unnecessary code, and eliminating failure paths rather than adding features.

models.title: Antifragility
models.description: Antifragile systems gain strength and improve from volatility, shocks, and stressors, whereas fragile systems break under stress.

models.title: Confirmation Bias
models.description: The tendency to search for, interpret, favor, and recall information in a way that confirms one's preexisting beliefs or hypotheses.

models.title: Sunk Cost Fallacy
models.description: Continuing an endeavor once an investment in money, effort, or time has been made, rather than evaluating forward-looking costs and benefits.

models.title: Survivorship Bias
models.description: Concentrating on the people or things that passed some selection process while overlooking those that did not, leading to false conclusions.

models.title: Incentive-Caused Bias
models.description: Never, ever, think about something else when you should be thinking about the power of incentives. People rationalize actions that benefit their wallet or status.

models.title: Hanlon's Razor
models.description: Never attribute to malice that which is adequately explained by neglect, miscommunication, or incompetence.

models.title: Gall's Law
models.description: A complex system that works is invariably found to have evolved from a simple system that worked. A complex system designed from scratch never works.

models.title: Conway's Law
models.description: Organizations that design systems are constrained to produce designs which are copies of the communication structures of these organizations.

models.title: Goodhart's Law
models.description: When a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure because participants alter their behavior to optimize for the proxy rather than the real goal.

models.title: The Pareto Principle (80/20 Rule)
models.description: For many outcomes, roughly 80% of consequences come from 20% of causes. Focus radically on the vital few inputs that generate the vast majority of value.

models.title: Occam's Razor
models.description: Entities should not be multiplied beyond necessity. When presented with competing hypotheses, choose the one that makes the fewest assumptions.
